claims.text: Reducing nanoribbon width enhances edge-induced strain gradients.
Reducing nanoribbon width increases shape-anisotropy effects.
Edge-induced strain gradients and shape anisotropy lower the energy barriers for magnetic domain-wall motion.
Lower domain-wall-motion barriers reduce magnetic hysteresis losses.
Lower domain-wall-motion barriers sharpen the low-field magnetocaloric response.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi film has a homogeneous microstructure.
Nanoribbons with widths of 50, 100, and 200 nm can serve as a controlled width series fabricated from the same as-deposited film.
The relevant magnetic transition is expected to occur approximately within 150–250 K.
Edge effects and boundary-induced strain gradients are the structural mediators of the width dependence.
Edge-induced strain modifies local magnetic anisotropy.
Modified local magnetic anisotropy eases domain-wall motion.
Easier domain-wall motion produces more reversible magnetization dynamics.
Narrower structures may provide enhanced thermal conduction that alleviates heat-transfer rate limitations during cooling cycles.
The 50 nm ribbons will exhibit lower magnetic hysteresis than wider ribbons and the unpatterned film.
The 50 nm ribbons will exhibit a more abrupt magnetocaloric entropy-change feature than wider ribbons and the unpatterned film.
The unpatterned baseline lacks the pronounced edge-induced strain gradients expected in patterned nanoribbons.
The proposed mechanism applies under fields below 100 Oe and near 150–250 K for FeMnNiGeSi nanoribbons on thermally robust substrates.
Substrate interactions and other nanoscale extrinsic factors may obscure the effect of ribbon width on magnetocaloric performance.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome text treats absent elevated edge strain or absent correlation with improved dynamics as falsifying, whereas the formal rule requires both lack of improved performance and lack of elevated edge strain. Thus, failure of performance despite confirmed elevated edge strain is not consistently classified.
